one_predeclared_consequence.name: Written participant ownership at a fixed later consumer
one_predeclared_consequence.nominal_rival_N: Both forms denote written participant references K and S. A paid frame must consume BOTH refs in declared slots, or relate them with an explicitly paid shared relation. If two physical instances/types are claimed, their distinction must actually be derived; two noun words alone do not establish it.
one_predeclared_consequence.topic_predicate_rival_V: OLKAIN is a named topic reference K; OLSHEDY is a unary event with an explicitly expressed patient reference. A paid generic topic-licensing relation must make that patient refer to K and consume the topic contribution. It cannot silently retain a spare nominal or give the event two patients.
one_predeclared_consequence.different_result: With a genuinely different S participant and a fixed later written consumer U, N supplies S to U whereas V supplies the explicitly bound K patient, or a separately written/paid material result of the event on K. Neither may pass an EventExpression directly into a MaterialRef slot.
one_predeclared_consequence.observable_falsifier: Freeze U arity, participant-type requirements, same-type identity policy and reference direction BEFORE role comparison. If U accepts only K-compatible material and the N reading supplies a genuinely incompatible S, N fails; the symmetric S-only constraint can falsify V. If U is generic or K/S are not differentiated, the roles remain observationally tied. A count of nouns/events or a fluent sentence is not the discriminator.
one_predeclared_consequence.anti_circularity: Do not assign U its restrictive type merely because the desired rival labels SHEDY a noun or verb. U must retain that same type/arity and lexical value in another fully consumed context that does not rely on this pair. Joint hypothetical bindings are permitted; confirmed external anchors are not prerequisites.
one_predeclared_consequence.current_status: Necessary nonnull participant/consumer bindings are not supplied by the present records. No complete context perspective meets this discriminator yet.
